source.title: Polyglot Teachers: Evaluating Language Models for Multilingual Synthetic Data Generation
source.citation: Lester James Validad Miranda et al., 2026
source.authors: Lester James Validad Miranda; Ivan Vulic; Anna Korhonen

record.tranche_reason: The study varies student-model and synthetic-data scale and reports downstream benchmark outcomes, conceptually testing downstream predictability with a different setup from pretraining scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit pretraining power laws, extrapolate loss from smaller pretraining runs, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its scale-related results concern supervised fine-tuning students and synthetic-data quantities. It also reports that intrinsic data-quality metrics predict student performance; this is recorded separately because the predictors are not scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The only result that bears on any version is the Tagalog ablation (Fig. 5). It scales the Gemma 3 student base from 4B to 12B to 27B under a fixed SFT recipe and reports FILBENCH scores, a weak three-point check of V6 in a new setting. No scaling law is fitted, and no pretraining loss, compute-optimal split or power-law form is measured. The SFT data-quantity sweep (App. G.1) is a control for PG-Score. It reports benchmark accuracy, not loss, and fits no functional form.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that teacher scale does not predict teacher effectiveness and that generated-data properties do. The data-scale sweep was a control showing that 10k examples suffice to compute PG-Score. In the Tagalog case study, larger students and more data give additional but smaller gains than teacher selection and family matching.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates multilingual synthetic-data generation and supervised fine-tuning, not the original pretraining-loss scaling-law procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The data-scale experiment reports diminishing performance gains beyond 10k examples; the Tagalog 10k-to-25k data increase yields a smaller gain than teacher selection or family matching.

fits_no_version.finding: Average multilingual benchmark performance of OLMo 3 7B students rises with SFT example count (1k to 50k), but gains diminish beyond 10k. On FILBENCH, going from 10k to 25k adds only 0.21 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream gains from more synthetic SFT data saturate around 10k examples in multilingual SFT, with a task-dependent saturation point.

fits_no_version.finding: Intrinsic data-quality PCs predict student performance (R²=0.664).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intrinsic synthetic-data quality metrics predict downstream student performance in multilingual SFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher log parameter size does not significantly predict PG-Score (β=0.053, p=0.507).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher parameter count alone does not predict multilingual synthetic-data teacher effectiveness.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The downstream scale findings concern multilingual SFT and a limited set of settings, not pretraining-loss scaling. The data-scale figure does not provide point values in the text; the Tagalog scale ablation is shown in a figure without uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scale-related result rows left out.

untested.parts: Whether gains follow a predictable functional form, whether they can be predicted from pretraining loss, and whether the result holds beyond three Gemma 3 sizes on one Tagalog benchmark.
Not tested: no pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small runs.
Not tested: SFT data scaling reports accuracy only, with no power-law loss fit.
Not tested: no comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 limits_scope label was removed because SFT data quantity with accuracy outcomes is not the scale or loss that V6 names. Those rows were moved to fits_no_version. The OLMo 3 32B result (App. G.2) reports only z-normalised PG-Scores, which cannot be compared to the 7B results as a scale effect, so it is not added.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating pretraining loss from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds beyond text pretraining. The study uses multilingual SFT, but does not test power-law loss behavior in that regime.

The study tests downstream benchmark outcomes when varying student model size and synthetic-data quantity in specific SFT settings. It does not test prediction from pretraining loss or establish a general scaling relationship across pretraining runs.
Dependence of pretraining-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, or bending of pretraining-loss curves.

relationships.condition: Gemma 3 base students (4B, 12B, 27B) SFT'd on the same 25k synthetic Tagalog data, evaluated on FILBENCH
relationships.reason: The FILBENCH score rises monotonically with student size, from 49.7 to 51.4 to 53.0 (r6, r7). There are only three points, with no fit or uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: FILBENCH scores increased from 49.7 to 51.4 to 53.0 as student size increased from 4B to 12B to 27B.
